text: Just like lists, dictionaries have their own comprehension syntax for building maps in one line.
The difference is the curly braces and a key-colon-value pair instead of a single expression.
So this builds a dictionary mapping each number to its square, instantly.
[chuckle] You can filter as you build, adding an if to keep only the even numbers and their squares.
A favorite trick is inverting a dictionary — swapping every key with its value.
[sigh] We loop over the items and simply flip the order, turning prices into a lookup by price.
And pairing it with zip is incredibly handy — zip stitches two lists together, item by item.
Here names and ages zip into a single dictionary of people, no loop needed.
[groan] Dict comprehensions turn what used to be a tedious loop-and-assign into one expressive line.
